title: Malignant Bowel Obstruction, Ascites & Palliative Care in Gynae-Oncology
subject: ss-gynaecological-oncology
refs: Berek & Hacker's Gynecologic Oncology 7th Edition Ch 26 (Palliative Care)
DeVita, Hellman, and Rosenberg's Cancer 11th Edition Ch 105 (Palliative Oncology)

steps.say: Malignant bowel obstruction represents one of the most distressing complications in advanced gynecologic oncology, developing in up to fifty percent of terminal ovarian cancer patients. Diffuse peritoneal carcinomatosis causes multifocal small bowel encasement, mesenteric foreshortening, and tumor infiltration of myenteric neural plexuses.
steps.tx: **Malignant bowel obstruction** (MBO) develops in 25% to 50% of advanced epithelial ovarian cancer patients, resulting from diffuse **peritoneal carcinomatosis**, mesenteric foreshortening, extensive serosal encasement, and neoplastic infiltration of the **myenteric autonomic plexus** causing dynamic intestinal hypomotility.  Evidence-based practice integrates malignant bowel obstruction (MBO), 25-50% terminal ovarian cancer, multi-segmental encasement.

steps.say: Computed tomography of the abdomen and pelvis with intravenous contrast serves as the definitive diagnostic imaging modality. CT imaging distinguishes a single-site focal mechanical blockage that might be surgically bypassable from diffuse, multifocal carcinomatosis where surgery is futile and contraindicated.
steps.tx: Contrast-enhanced **computed tomography** of the abdomen and pelvis is the gold standard imaging investigation for MBO, essential for differentiating a focal, isolated **mechanical obstruction** (potentially amenable to surgical resection or enterostomy) from multifocal, inoperable **peritoneal carcinomatosis**.  Evidence-based practice integrates CT imaging for MBO, single-site vs multifocal, inoperable carcinomatosis.

steps.say: Medical management represents the primary treatment for inoperable malignant bowel obstruction. A continuous subcutaneous or intravenous infusion combining the somatostatin analogue octreotide, haloperidol, and dexamethasone effectively controls nausea, pain, and gastrointestinal hypersecretion.
steps.tx: First-line medical therapy for inoperable MBO utilizes a continuous infusion combining **octreotide** (300 to 600 mcg/day, reducing gastrointestinal secretomotor activity and luminal distension), **haloperidol** (antiemetic targeting the chemoreceptor trigger zone), and **dexamethasone** (6 to 8 mg/day to reduce peritumoral edema).  Evidence-based practice integrates octreotide 300-600 mcg/day, dexamethasone anti-edema.

rows: Somatostatin analogue; inhibits GI fluid secretion

steps.say: Prokinetic agents such as metoclopramide are strictly contraindicated in patients with complete mechanical bowel obstruction. Stimulating intestinal motility against an impassable physical blockage generates excruciating colicky pain, escalates intraluminal pressure, and risks bowel perforation.
steps.tx: Prokinetic medications such as **metoclopramide** are **strictly contraindicated** in complete mechanical bowel obstruction, as prokinetic stimulation of peristalsis against a closed obstruction produces excruciating colic, severe abdominal pain, and substantially elevates the catastrophic risk of **bowel perforation**.  Evidence-based practice integrates contraindication to metoclopramide, complete obstruction, bowel perforation risk.

left.title: Metoclopramide Contraindicated
points: Induces severe pain, distension, and transmural bowel perforation

right.title: Metoclopramide Indicated
points: Indicated in partial functional hypomotility without blockage
Useful in gastroparesis and opioid-induced bowel inertia

steps.say: Percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy placement serves as an outstanding minimally invasive decompression procedure for patients with refractory inoperable malignant bowel obstruction. Venting gastrostomy eliminates relentless feculent vomiting and permits discontinuation of painful nasogastric tubes.
steps.tx: A **venting gastrostomy** or **percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy** (PEG) tube provides highly effective palliation for refractory inoperable MBO, decompressing accumulated gastric secretions, eliminating feculent vomiting, and permitting removal of uncomfortable nasogastric tubes in >90% of terminal patients.  Evidence-based practice integrates venting gastrostomy (PEG), vomiting relief >90%, elimination of nasogastric tube.

nodes.label: Document refractory vomiting in inoperable MBO despite medical therapy
Temporarily decompress stomach with fine-bore nasogastric tube
Perform percutaneous endoscopic gastrostomy (PEG) under mild sedation
Open tube to passive gravity drainage; allow patient pleasure sips

steps.say: Recurrent symptomatic malignant ascites causes distressing abdominal distension, anorexia, and dyspnea in advanced ovarian carcinoma. Indwelling tunneled peritoneal drainage catheters permit safe, intermittent, home-based drainage, avoiding repeated hospital visits for large-volume paracentesis.
steps.tx: Recurrent **malignant ascites** is safely palliated with **indwelling tunneled peritoneal catheters** (such as PleurX), which enable patient-directed, intermittent home drainage of peritoneal fluid (typically 1 to 1.5 liters per session), effectively eliminating the need for frequent, stressful hospital paracentesis visits.  Evidence-based practice integrates tunneled peritoneal catheter (PleurX).

left.title: Tunneled Peritoneal Catheter
points: Subcutaneous polyester cuff prevents bacterial migration
Enables safe home drainage by family/caregivers
Prevents severe ascites reaccumulation and dyspnea

right.title: Repeated Serial Paracentesis
points: Requires recurrent outpatient or emergency admissions
Repeated abdominal wall punctures risk bowel puncture
Causes rapid fluid shifts and hemodynamic instability

steps.say: Catumaxomab is a bispecific trifunctional antibody targeting epithelial cell adhesion molecule and cluster of differentiation three. Administered via intraperitoneal infusion, catumaxomab binds tumor cells and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, destroying intraperitoneal tumor cells and extending puncture-free survival.
steps.tx: **Catumaxomab** is a bispecific trifunctional monoclonal antibody targeting **EpCAM** on ovarian cancer cells and **CD3** on T lymphocytes, while recruiting Fc-gamma-receptor accessory immune cells to eliminate intraperitoneal tumor seeding and significantly prolong **puncture-free survival** in malignant ascites.  Evidence-based practice integrates bispecific antibody (anti-EpCAM x anti-CD3).

rows: Binds surface of malignant ovarian cancer cells
Directs antibody specifically to cancer cells
CD3 receptor on mature T cells
Crosslinks and activates cytotoxic T lymphocytes
Fc-gamma receptor I/IIa/III on macrophages/NK cells
Recruits natural killer cells and macrophages

steps.say: Severe neuropathic pelvic pain from neoplastic invasion of the lumbosacral plexus requires multimodal analgesic therapy with scheduled opioid titration and adjuvant neuromodulators. For refractory visceral pain, image-guided superior hypogastric plexus neurolysis provides effective and durable pain relief.
steps.tx: Severe **neuropathic pelvic pain** from neoplastic lumbosacral plexus infiltration requires multimodal therapy combining scheduled opioids with adjuvant neuromodulators (**gabapentin**, pregabalin, duloxetine); percutaneous **superior hypogastric plexus block** achieves substantial neurolytic visceral pelvic pain relief.  Evidence-based practice integrates gabapentinoids and opioids. Comprehensive multidisciplinary review ensures optimal patient survival outcomes.

nodes.label: Identify intractable neuropathic or visceral pelvic pain
Titrate scheduled long-acting opioids with breakthrough doses
Perform fluoroscopy-guided superior hypogastric plexus block
